lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: defining sine, cosine, and tangent

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: From a point 42 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 40 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
A right triangle has legs 10 and 24 and hypotenuse 26. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 10. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
A right triangle has hypotenuse 125 and one leg 35. Find the other leg.
Express sin 46° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 44°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 46°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 134°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 136°, because the angles differ by a right angle

items.prompt: From a point 63 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 60 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 24 and 45 and hypotenuse 51. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 24. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
